Round-trip verified against real usage-pulse repo. Codex + Kimi registrars match documented shapes; Claude registrar writes internal cache file installed_plugins.json instead of the documented marketplace.json path — needs refactor. next_steps.title: Rewrite ClaudeRegistrar to use marketplace.json
next_steps.detail: Per official docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces), Claude's documented install path is a marketplace descriptor + `claude plugin install <name>@<marketplace>`. Current ClaudeRegistrar in src/plugin_forge/registrars.py writes directly to ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json (internal cache, undocumented). Refactor: emit ~/.forge-local/marketplace.json listing every forge-managed plugin with { name, source: <install_dir>, description, version }; do NOT touch installed_plugins.json. Optional: subprocess-invoke `claude plugin install <name>@forge-local` after marketplace registration.

next_steps.title: Verify Codex registrar output against a real config.toml
next_steps.detail: Current CodexRegistrar writes `source = str(install_dir.parent)` — should probably point at the marketplace root not the individual plugin. Compare against the live `[marketplaces.0langas-personal]` block in ~/.codex/config.toml (source_type=local, source=<0langas-plugin-marketplace root>). Also verify that install_path is not a documented field on [plugins."name@mkt"] — the docs only show `enabled = true` there.

next_steps.title: Kimi registrar copies files vs points at source
next_steps.detail: Docs say `Local installations are copied to $KIMI_CODE_HOME/plugins/managed/<id>/, and the CLI always runs from this managed copy.` Current KimiRegistrar writes root=<install_dir> where install_dir is forge's copy target. Needs to verify Kimi CLI accepts a `local-path` install where root points at any dir, or whether it must live under managed/. Check the shape used by other 0langas plugins in ~/.kimi-code/plugins/installed.json (RECALL entry uses root under managed/ and originalSource under repos/).

next_steps.title: Live install one plugin end-to-end
next_steps.detail: Once above 3 are done, install usage-pulse via forge into all 3 providers on this machine and confirm: hooks fire, MCP registered, /pulse works. Rollback via forge uninstall must be byte-clean (compare backups).

next_steps.title: Fix Claude hooks.json shape
next_steps.detail: Adapters emit flat {event, command, matcher, timeout}. Claude's real hooks.json shape (per docs) nests: { "hooks": { "PostToolUse": [{ "matcher": "Write|Edit", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "..." }] }] } }. Update src/plugin_forge/adapters/_common.py render_hook_entries + writers in claude.py and codex.py.

next_steps.title: CI file cannot be pushed by current PAT
next_steps.detail: docs/ci.yml.pending-workflow-scope is a valid GH Actions workflow (matrix ubuntu+windows, py3.11-3.13, ruff+pytest+coverage). Token used by gh CLI lacks `workflow` scope so any push touching .github/workflows/* is rejected. Fix: either add workflow scope to the PAT and rename+push, or upload the file through github.com UI once. File contents intentionally moved out of .github/workflows/ so main-branch pushes succeed.

next_steps.title: Fix installed.json path assumption in tests
next_steps.detail: tests/test_registrars.py monkeypatches Path.home() which works but the Kimi registrar hard-codes `~/.kimi-code/plugins/installed.json`. Real path on this machine is confirmed correct. Should still be checked for macOS/Linux equivalence — Kimi's XDG path might differ.

blockers.description: PAT missing `workflow` scope. Blocks pushing GH Actions workflow file.
blockers.workaround: docs/ci.yml.pending-workflow-scope; move to .github/workflows/ci.yml manually after token is upgraded or via web UI.
